page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 768.0 GB, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 5669 GB of capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several key areas. The server achieves top 10% placement in Passmark CPU scores, database operations, and static web serving throughput, which reached 136.17 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with uncached large-block read speeds at 506.7 GB/sec and write speeds at 207.77 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall within the top 25%. Advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) are present, contributing to strong performance in extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E96ds_v6 offers a dense allocation of memory and high-capacity local storage relative to its 96 vCPUs, making it a viable option for resource-heavy deployments without requiring dedicated hardware. The combination of high memory bandwidth, substantial local storage, and strong multi-core performance makes this server highly suitable for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
